findings.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup registration uses the literal alias "alias" instead of the actual created alias "idp-alias-" + i, so `testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")` returns a 404-facing resource whose `remove()` is invoked on a nonexistent provider. All 20 created IDPs leak into the realm (and the organization links on idp-alias-10..19 leak too), so the test realm accumulates state that breaks subsequent tests' count-based assertions like `assertEquals(5, ...getIDPs("").size())` in later runs/orderings, and the cleanup hook itself throws when it removes a nonexistent resource.

[ADVISORY] The second (searchKey-miss) cache write passes `cache.getCurrentCounter()` to `addRevisioned` instead of the `startupRevision` used on the first-population path at line ~231, producing inconsistent revision bookkeeping for the same cache key within one session. The rebuilt query object is stamped with the cache's current counter rather than the session's startup revision, so a concurrent invalidation registered during this session (registered against revisions between startupRevision and current) can end up not evicting the freshly-cached login IDP list, serving stale login IDPs until the next unrelated invalidation.

[ADVISORY] Cache resolution of the cached IDP set goes through `session.identityProviders().getById(id)`, i.e. the same caching provider, so a cached login list containing an IDP whose per-ID cache entry was individually invalidated but whose list cache was not will return null and force a full delegate reload on every call, permanently thrashing until some other operation invalidates the list key. Any code path that invalidates the per-IDP cache entry (e.g. `registerIDPInvalidation`) without also invalidating the login list key — such as the alias-update branch of `update()` when the IDP qualifies for login and org link is unchanged — leaves the login cache pointing at IDs whose individual entries are marked invalid, causing repeated delegate round-trips on every login page render.

[ADVISORY] The new predicate arm dereferences `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` without a null check on `getConfig()`, unlike `IdentityProviderModel` callers that assume config is always initialized. Any caller constructing an `IdentityProviderModel` without initializing its config map (possible for custom storage providers or tests) hits a NullPointerException inside `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)`, which is now invoked unconditionally on every create/update/remove through `registerIDPLoginInvalidation`.

[BUG] In `remove(alias)`, `storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` is fetched before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)`, so the cached branch now always performs a delegate (uncached, DB) lookup on every removal, defeating the point of the cached-alias fast path the original code guarded with `isInvalid`. Every IDP removal, including hot admin and self-registration broker cleanup paths, now unconditionally hits the underlying store even when the alias was resolvable from the invalidation-avoidance cache branch, a hot-path regression on the previously guarded path.

[BUG] On the cache-hit and cache-population paths, getForLogin resolves cached IDs via session.identityProviders().getById(id) and returns the results raw, without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both the isInvalid path and the idp == null fallback path do wrap. Organization-linked IDPs served from a warm login cache are returned as plain CachedIdentityProvider models instead of organization-aware models, so org-scoped login behavior (identity provider visibility/redirect handling that depends on the org-aware wrapper) silently differs depending on whether the cache is warm, producing nondeterministic login pages across nodes.

[BUG] The cleanup registration calls testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove with the literal alias "alias", which matches no existing identity provider, so get("alias") returns null and the method reference dereference throws NPE (or the cleanup silently removes nothing for the correct IDPs). testCacheIDPForLogin fails with a NullPointerException during setup at the first get("alias") call (no IDP with alias "alias" exists), and even if it survived, the 20 created providers would never be cleaned up, polluting subsequent tests in the realm.

[ADVISORY] The invalidation test never exercises removal of an IDP that currently qualifies for login: step 1 removes idp-alias-1 (disabled, non-login) and the hideOnLogin creation is non-login, so the registerIDPLoginInvalidation branch in remove() that fires for a login IDP has no coverage. A regression where remove() of an enabled, login-visible IDP fails to invalidate the login caches (stale IDP offered on the login page after deletion) would pass the entire test suite; the test only asserts the negative branch (non-login removal leaves caches intact).

[ADVISORY] The test populates cache entries only for the organizationId values used (null and orgaId) and never exercises the query != null && cached == null branch of getForLogin where a second, different organizationId is requested against an existing cache entry. The chained-query path (invalidateObject + addRevisioned with getCurrentCounter) is completely untested; if the chaining/counter logic drops the previously cached searchKey or produces a revision that never validates, multiple-organization realms would get empty or stale login IDP lists with no test catching it.

[ADVISORY] update() calls registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpById, model) where idpById comes from getById(model.getInternalId()) and can be null when the internal ID does not resolve, and the organization-link comparison Objects.equals(original.getOrganizationId(), updated.getOrganizationId()) then dereferences the null original after the first predicate short-circuit only saves the second check when original is non-null-but-not-login. If getById returns null for a model whose update path reaches the second if-block, getOrganizationId() throws NPE — and more importantly the null-original case (IDP updated via a model built without the full stored state) skips login invalidation entirely because getLoginPredicate().test(null) is false, leaving stale login caches.

[BUG] On a cache hit, getForLogin returns raw models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both delegate paths (invalid cache key and cache miss) wrap every model. A user gets organization-aware (login-redirect-URI-adjusted) IDP models on the first login page request and unwrapped models on every subsequent request served from cache, producing visibly different login behavior (e.g., wrong redirect targets or org-scoped fields) depending on whether the cache is warm — exactly the class of inconsistency the cache layer exists to prevent.

[ADVISORY] The PR titled 'add caching support for getForLogin' silently changes the SPI's LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate semantics for every implementation, adding a global filter that excludes organization-linked non-public IDPs. Non-cached implementations (JPA storage, custom SPI implementations) change behavior at runtime from this diff with no requirement traceable to the stated caching intent; anyone relying on getForLogin returning org-linked private brokers (or a downstream Keycloak version diffing behavior) is bitten without any mention in the PR's stated scope. This belongs in its own, documented change.

[ADVISORY] The added isEnabled() re-filter with the comment 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped' is a symptom-patching workaround unrelated to caching rather than a fix of the wrapper that loses the enabled flag. The underlying wrapper (createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel) that drops/mutes the enabled state remains in place and will silently break any other consumer of getForLogin results that does not re-check isEnabled; future callers of the cached path get a model that misreports enabled, and the invariant 'a cached and uncached model are equivalent' is not enforced anywhere.

[BUG] The two cache-population branches use inconsistent revision bookkeeping: the cold path calls cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision) while the add-a-new-searchKey path calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) then cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()). The addRevisioned with startupRevision on the cold path can pin the entry to a stale revision, so a subsequent invalidation registered via registerIDPInvalidation (which bumps the current revision) does not evict the entry created after it in a race, serving a stale login IDP list on the next getForLogin call.

[BUG] The test cleanup registers testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, but no IDP with alias "alias" exists (the created aliases are "idp-alias-N"), so get("alias") returns null and the method reference throws NullPointerException during cleanup. Test cleanup aborts with an NPE, leaving the 20 created IDPs in the realm and failing/cascading failures in subsequent tests in the class.

[BUG] The cached path in getForLogin resolves IDPs via session.identityProviders().getById(id), which returns the raw CachedIdentityProvider without the organization-aware wrapping that both delegate-return paths apply via createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so warm-cache results differ from cold-cache results for ORG_ONLY/ALL fetches. A login page rendered after the cache is populated shows IDPs with different behavior than one rendered before caching: organization-specific display config, alias handling, and the enabled re-check the OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean now depends on (its new isEnabled filter exists precisely because wrapped models can be disabled) are all skipped, so disabled org-linked IDPs appear on the org login page on warm requests and disappear on cold ones.

[BUG] Both cleanup registrations use the literal alias "alias" (testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) instead of the created alias "idp-alias-" + i, so every one of the 21 created IDPs is registered for cleanup under a nonexistent alias. get("alias") returns null and the method reference throws NPE during test cleanup (or silently removes nothing), leaving 21 orphaned IDPs in the shared TEST_REALM_NAME that pollute every subsequent test in the suite; the test itself passes while the realm is left corrupted.

[BUG] The two cache-population branches use inconsistent revisions for addRevisioned: the first-load branch passes startupRevision while the miss-for-new-searchKey branch passes cache.getCurrentCounter(), so the same key can be written with a stale revision relative to invalidations that already occurred. After an invalidation, a subsequent first-load on a node that started before the invalidation re-adds the query with the old startupRevision, resurrecting the pre-invalidation entry so stale IDP lists (e.g. listing an IDP deleted via remove(), which registerIDPLoginInvalidation already invalidated) are served for login until the next full invalidation — stale login IDPs shown to end users.

[ADVISORY] The caching PR silently changes getLoginPredicate() semantics for every implementation (JPA, LDAP, cache) by excluding org-linked IDPs that lack BROKER_PUBLIC, a behavioral change to the login IDP selection contract, not just to cache behavior. Any existing caller of getLoginPredicate()/getForLogin (login page, backchannel logout, admin console IDP listing, custom storage providers) that previously saw org-linked non-public IDPs no longer does after this diff, with no interface versioning or changelog; deployments relying on org-linked IDPs appearing in FetchMode.ALL results change behavior on upgrade.

[ADVISORY] The per-(realm,mode) login cache entry accumulates one embedded searchKey set per organization ever queried, and every query for an organization not yet in the entry does cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) plus a full delegate reload, so in a realm with N organizations the first login page hit per org invalidates and rebuilds the shared entry N times. Realms with many organizations get repeated full IDP reloads (one per new org) and a single unbounded cache value whose size grows with org count and never shrinks; the invalidateObject is also node-local, so concurrent cluster nodes racing to add different searchKeys with parent-based overwrites lose each other's entries, causing repeated cold reloads.

[ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) (an uncached delegate hit) even on the previously cache-served path, adding a storage round-trip to every IDP removal. Every remove() on any node pays an extra delegate lookup; more importantly the fetched storedIdp is passed to registerIDPLoginInvalidation, and if the alias key was cached-and-stale relative to the org link the predicate test runs against the wrong org state, deciding invalidation on outdated data.

[BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both cache-miss paths apply it, producing different results for identical queries depending on cache state. On the first (uncached) request the caller receives organization-aware wrapped IDP models (with org-specific config/behavior), and on every subsequent cached request it receives unwrapped delegate models, so login page behavior (e.g. organization-scoped broker config) silently changes between the first and later requests until invalidation — a direct intent drift for a caching layer whose contract is transparency.

[BUG] In create(), registerIDPLoginInvalidation evaluates getLoginPredicate() on the incoming model, whose OrganizationId is set only after the organization provider links it via OrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider / the org update path that bypasses this provider's update() (the org link mutates the IDP through the organization API), so no invalidation of the login caches occurs when an existing IDP is linked to or unlinked from an organization. Linking/unlinking an IDP to an organization through the organization management API leaves stale getForLogin caches: FetchMode.ORG_ONLY/ALL queries keep returning (or omitting) the IDP until some unrelated invalidation, so organization login pages show stale broker lists; the test only passes because step 4 mutates BROKER_PUBLIC config (which does invalidate) immediately before addIdentityProvider.

[BUG] The new predicate conjunct dereferences idp.getConfig().get(...) without a null guard, and the same lambda is also executed in registerIDPLoginInvalidation on the create() path where a caller-supplied model can carry a null config map. An IdentityProviderModel with a null config (constructible via constructor without config) causes NullPointerException inside getLoginPredicate wherever the filter is applied (e.g. getForLogin on any storage provider, or the cache provider's create/update invalidation), breaking IDP creation and login queries with a 500.

[BUG] The cleanup registration uses the literal alias "alias" instead of the actual alias "idp-alias-" + i, so the cleanup closure fetches a nonexistent resource for every created IDP. Test teardown calls remove() on an IdentityProviderResource for a nonexistent alias, producing a 404/exception during cleanup and leaking all 20+ created IDPs between tests in the realm, which corrupts subsequent count-based assertions.

[ADVISORY] The new predicate link dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null check, so any IdentityProviderModel with a null config map throws NullPointerException when getForLogin is invoked. The login predicate is applied to every IdentityProviderModel returned from storage on every getForLogin call; an IDP persisted without a config map (or a storage provider returning a model with null config) turns the realm's login page into a 500 error, a denial of the entire login flow for that realm. The legacy filters never dereferenced config unconditionally here, so this is newly introduced on this line.

[ADVISORY] getForLogin caches per-(realm, FetchMode) but stores results for an unbounded set of organizationIds in one IdentityProviderListQuery under a key that does not include the organizationId, and on a cache hit the stored set is served without any re-validation that the IDPs are still login-eligible. A realm with many organizations accumulates per-org ID lists in a single shared cache entry; more importantly, if any mutation path updates an IDP through a code path that does not route through InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.update/remove/create (e.g., organization link changes performed directly against the delegate or via bulk import/migration), stale cached lists serve disabled or org-private (BROKER_PUBLIC=false) brokers on the public login page, exposing identity-provider metadata the admin intended to hide and letting users initiate logins with providers that were disabled for the org. The invalidation logic in registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate is only consulted on the update() path of this wrapper, so the cache correctness for login visibility is only as strong as that single choke point.

[BUG] The cleanup registration looks up IDP alias "alias", which does not exist, instead of "idp-alias-" + i. testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") returns null, so the method reference ::remove throws NullPointerException during test cleanup — and none of the 20 created IDPs are actually removed, polluting the realm for subsequent tests in the class. Same bug repeats at the idp-alias-20 creation site (~line 419).

[BUG] Every getForLogin() call in the test discards its return value; the test asserts only internal cache-query sizes, never the contents of the stream getForLogin returns. If getForLogin returns the wrong providers (e.g., disabled IDPs included because createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel loses the enabled flag, or wrong FetchMode filtering, or wrong org mapping), the test still passes — it verifies the cache machinery, not the cached behavior the PR claims to add. The assertEquals(5/10/11, query.getIDPs(...).size()) assertions are performed on the cache object, a mirror of the implementation's internal representation, not on the API contract.

[ADVISORY] The stale-cache-entry fallback branch in getForLogin (cached id resolves to a null IDP → invalidate cacheKey and re-delegate) has no test triggering it. A regression in this recovery path (e.g., infinite inconsistency or wrong invalidation) would ship unverified; the only test in the diff (OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin) never leaves a dangling internalId in the cache. Checked: testsuite/integration-arquillian/.../cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java is the only test file in the diff and never exercises this branch.

[ADVISORY] The multi-search branch (query exists but query.getIDPs(searchKey) returns null for a new searchKey, triggering invalidateObject + re-load with the old query as parent) is never exercised by the new test. Every test call uses one searchKey per FetchMode ("" for REALM_ONLY, orgaId for ORG_ONLY/ALL), so the branch that merges a second search result into an existing IdentityProviderListQuery is untested; a defect there (e.g., wrong revision counter passed to addRevisioned — note it uses cache.getCurrentCounter() while the first path uses startupRevision) only manifests in production when a realm serves two different organizations, and operators get stale or missing IDP lists on the login page.

[ADVISORY] The new LoginFilter predicate clause excluding org-linked IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC is verified only for the positive case; the diff's test links only BROKER_PUBLIC=true IDPs to the organization, so no test asserts an org-linked, non-public IDP is (or is not) excluded from any FetchMode. The semantic change that a non-public org broker is now hidden even from FetchMode.REALM_ONLY/ALL listings is untested; if the intended behavior differs per FetchMode (e.g., REALM_ONLY should still surface it for email-domain matching on the realm login page), no test in this diff would catch it. Checked OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin — it creates no org-linked, non-BROKER_PUBLIC IDP.

[ADVISORY] Step 2 (non-availability-changing updates) asserts only that the login cache entries still exist, never that a subsequent getForLogin returns the updated IDP data (e.g., the trustEmail/config change) read through the surviving cache. If the skipped login-cache invalidation combined with per-IDP cache staleness returned outdated IDP models, this test passes because it never re-invokes getForLogin after the update; the caching-correctness guarantee the PR's javadoc for registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate claims ("no need to invalidate" implies data stays correct) is asserted only via cache-object presence, not via behavior.

[BUG] On a cache hit, getForLogin returns raw models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so cached and uncached code paths return different model types. The two cold paths (isInvalid branch and the idp==null fallback) wrap each model with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, but the cache-hit loop at lines ~246-252 does not; once the login list query is cached, login pages served from cache receive non-organization-aware IdentityProviderModel instances while the first request after invalidation receives wrapped ones — any behavior that depends on the wrapper (org-specific presentation/config) silently differs depending on whether the cache is warm, producing intermittent, unreproducible login-page behavior.

[ADVISORY] The new predicate dereferences idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) without a null guard, and the predicate now silently swallows the org-linked check when BROKER_PUBLIC is set to any non-'true' string. For an IDP with organizationId != null and a null config map (IdentityProviderModel.getConfig returns null when unset in some storage/load paths), getLoginPredicate throws NPE inside getForLogin, registerIDPLoginInvalidation, and registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate — breaking IDP create/update/remove operations with a 500. Additionally, Boolean.parseBoolean means config values like "TRUE " or a legacy non-canonical value silently exclude an IDP the admin believes is public, with no log or error; the IDP just disappears from login with no diagnostic.

[ADVISORY] In remove(), the stored IDP is fetched via idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) before checking isInvalid(cacheKey), but the registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) on line ~112 only fires when the currently-stored model still satisfies getLoginPredicate, which reads through the delegate — and the predicate's new BROKER_PUBLIC clause means an org-linked IDP whose BROKER_PUBLIC config is absent is treated as not-a-login-IDP and its removal skips login-cache invalidation. Removing an org-linked IDP that was previously returned by getForLogin(FetchMode.ALL/ORG_ONLY) via a path where BROKER_PUBLIC was true at cache-population time but the predicate now evaluates it as ineligible leaves stale internal IDs in the login list query; the cached path's getById==null fallback mitigates it, but only after the cache is read and the fallback triggers a delegate reload — meanwhile getIDPs() consumers of the cached query (and any cross-node replica where the invalidation hasn't propagated) observe the removed IDP as present until then.

From the diff alone, it’s clear there is a potential NPE if a non-null `IdentityProviderModel` instance can have a null config map, but the diff does not establish whether `IdentityProviderModel#getConfig()` is always non-null by contract, so the defect cannot be conclusively verified here.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `remove(String alias)` to unconditionally execute `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)`. Previously, when the alias cache key was valid, the method could use the cached entry (`realmCache.getCache().get(cacheKey, CachedIdentityProvider.class)`) to determine what to invalidate without consulting the delegate. The new code forces a delegate lookup even on the cached fast path, which is a concrete performance/caching regression visible in the diff, but it does not demonstrably break correctness (it still invalidates and removes).

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `getForLogin` implementation, the cache-miss/invalid paths return `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, but the cache-hit path resolves IDs via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns `identityProviders.stream()` without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` (see the loop building `identityProviders`). This means results can differ depending on whether the login list is served from the warm cache vs recomputed, and the diff itself indicates the wrapper is required for login lists (it is explicitly applied on the other paths).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup registration calls testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove with the literal alias "alias", which matches no existing identity provider, so get("alias") returns null and the method reference dereference throws NPE (or the cleanup silently removes nothing for the correct IDPs). testCacheIDPForLogin fails with a NullPointerException during setup at the first get("alias") call (no IDP with alias "alias" exists), and even if it survived, the 20 created providers would never be cleaned up, polluting subsequent tests in the realm.

adjudication.rationale: In the new testCacheIDPForLogin loop, after creating each IDP with alias `idp-alias-<i>`, the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (literal string "alias"). This does not correspond to any of the created providers’ aliases, so the cleanup will not remove the created IDPs and can pollute subsequent tests. The finding’s NPE-at-setup detail is not guaranteed from the diff (the admin client may return a non-null resource proxy), but the cleanup target is clearly incorrect and thus a real defect in the added test code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The invalidation test never exercises removal of an IDP that currently qualifies for login: step 1 removes idp-alias-1 (disabled, non-login) and the hideOnLogin creation is non-login, so the registerIDPLoginInvalidation branch in remove() that fires for a login IDP has no coverage. A regression where remove() of an enabled, login-visible IDP fails to invalidate the login caches (stale IDP offered on the login page after deletion) would pass the entire test suite; the test only asserts the negative branch (non-login removal leaves caches intact).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new invalidation behavior in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove()` via `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`, which only invalidates when `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)` is true. In the new `testCacheIDPForLogin()` step (1), the only removal is `idp-alias-1` which was created with `setEnabled((i % 2) == 0)` and therefore is disabled (non-login), and the newly created `idp-alias-20` is `hideOnLogin=true` (also non-login). Subsequent steps exercise updates that change login availability but never remove an IDP that qualifies for login. So the test suite does not cover the positive invalidation branch on deletion, and a regression where deleting an enabled/login-visible IDP fails to invalidate login caches would not be caught by this test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The test populates cache entries only for the organizationId values used (null and orgaId) and never exercises the query != null && cached == null branch of getForLogin where a second, different organizationId is requested against an existing cache entry. The chained-query path (invalidateObject + addRevisioned with getCurrentCounter) is completely untested; if the chaining/counter logic drops the previously cached searchKey or produces a revision that never validates, multiple-organization realms would get empty or stale login IDP lists with no test catching it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial caching logic in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin()`. Specifically, when a cache entry (`IdentityProviderListQuery query`) exists but does not contain results for a new `searchKey` (`cached = query.getIDPs(searchKey)` returns null), it executes the “chained-query” path: `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)`, then rebuilds `query = new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)` and stores it via `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. The new test `testCacheIDPForLogin()` only ever calls `getForLogin(...)` with `organizationId` values of `null` (mapped to `searchKey = ""`) and a single `orgaId`, so it never triggers the `query != null && cached == null` branch for a *second different* organizationId against an existing cache entry. That means this newly added chaining/revision-counter behavior is untested, which is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap (not necessarily a proven defect).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] update() calls registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpById, model) where idpById comes from getById(model.getInternalId()) and can be null when the internal ID does not resolve, and the organization-link comparison Objects.equals(original.getOrganizationId(), updated.getOrganizationId()) then dereferences the null original after the first predicate short-circuit only saves the second check when original is non-null-but-not-login. If getById returns null for a model whose update path reaches the second if-block, getOrganizationId() throws NPE — and more importantly the null-original case (IDP updated via a model built without the full stored state) skips login invalidation entirely because getLoginPredicate().test(null) is false, leaving stale login caches.

adjudication.rationale: The claimed NPE in registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate is not supported by the diff: getLoginPredicate() is explicitly guarded with Objects::nonNull, so getLoginPredicate().test(original) is false when original is null, and the second if-block only dereferences original.getOrganizationId() when getLoginPredicate().test(original) is true (therefore original is non-null). Also, a null original does not “skip login invalidation entirely” in general: if updated qualifies for login, the method falls through to the invalidation loop. The only early-return case with original==null is when updated also does not qualify for login, and the diff alone doesn’t establish that getById can be null in a valid update path or that this leads to stale caches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] On a cache hit, getForLogin returns raw models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both delegate paths (invalid cache key and cache miss) wrap every model. A user gets organization-aware (login-redirect-URI-adjusted) IDP models on the first login page request and unwrapped models on every subsequent request served from cache, producing visibly different login behavior (e.g., wrong redirect targets or org-scoped fields) depending on whether the cache is warm — exactly the class of inconsistency the cache layer exists to prevent.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`, the delegate paths (`isInvalid(cacheKey)` and cache population branches) return `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, ensuring wrapping. However, on a cache hit it reconstructs results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns `identityProviders.stream()` without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` (or any equivalent wrapping) to those models. This creates an observable inconsistency between cold-cache vs warm-cache behavior, exactly as described in the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The PR titled 'add caching support for getForLogin' silently changes the SPI's LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate semantics for every implementation, adding a global filter that excludes organization-linked non-public IDPs. Non-cached implementations (JPA storage, custom SPI implementations) change behavior at runtime from this diff with no requirement traceable to the stated caching intent; anyone relying on getForLogin returning org-linked private brokers (or a downstream Keycloak version diffing behavior) is bitten without any mention in the PR's stated scope. This belongs in its own, documented change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes SPI-wide semantics in `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding a new global predicate: `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`. This affects every `getForLogin(...)` implementation (including non-cached ones), not just the new Infinispan caching added in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin(...)`. That is a real, diff-grounded scope/behavior change concern, even if it may be intended; it’s not inherently a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The added isEnabled() re-filter with the comment 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped' is a symptom-patching workaround unrelated to caching rather than a fix of the wrapper that loses the enabled flag. The underlying wrapper (createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel) that drops/mutes the enabled state remains in place and will silently break any other consumer of getForLogin results that does not re-check isEnabled; future callers of the cached path get a model that misreports enabled, and the invariant 'a cached and uncached model are equivalent' is not enforced anywhere.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows an added `filter(idp -> idp.isEnabled() ...)` in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` with a comment about wrapping, but it does not show the implementation of `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` or any evidence that it “drops/mutes” the enabled flag. Additionally, the new cached `getForLogin` path in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider` returns `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` results (no wrapping there), so the claim that “future callers of the cached path get a model that misreports enabled” is not supported by what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The two cache-population branches use inconsistent revision bookkeeping: the cold path calls cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision) while the add-a-new-searchKey path calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) then cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()). The addRevisioned with startupRevision on the cold path can pin the entry to a stale revision, so a subsequent invalidation registered via registerIDPInvalidation (which bumps the current revision) does not evict the entry created after it in a race, serving a stale login IDP list on the next getForLogin call.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show inconsistent revision/counter arguments when populating the new login cache in getForLogin(): the initial population path does `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, while the “new searchKey” path does `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and then `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. That inconsistency is verifiable from the diff and could matter depending on how RealmCacheManager interprets the second argument. However, the specific claim that using `startupRevision` will cause an entry to survive later invalidations and serve stale data cannot be confirmed from this diff alone because the semantics of `addRevisioned`, `startupRevision`, and revision invalidation are not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The test cleanup registers testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, but no IDP with alias "alias" exists (the created aliases are "idp-alias-N"), so get("alias") returns null and the method reference throws NullPointerException during cleanup. Test cleanup aborts with an NPE, leaving the 20 created IDPs in the realm and failing/cascading failures in subsequent tests in the class.

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `testCacheIDPForLogin`, after creating IDPs with aliases like `"idp-alias-" + i` (and later `"idp-alias-20"`), the cleanup registers `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` twice. The literal string "alias" does not match any of the created aliases, so cleanup will attempt to remove the wrong IDP and likely fail (e.g., 404/exception), leaving the created IDPs behind and potentially breaking subsequent tests. The finding’s core issue (incorrect cleanup alias) is directly verifiable from the diff, though the specific claim about `get("alias")` returning null/NPE is not guaranteed by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cached path in getForLogin resolves IDPs via session.identityProviders().getById(id), which returns the raw CachedIdentityProvider without the organization-aware wrapping that both delegate-return paths apply via createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so warm-cache results differ from cold-cache results for ORG_ONLY/ALL fetches. A login page rendered after the cache is populated shows IDPs with different behavior than one rendered before caching: organization-specific display config, alias handling, and the enabled re-check the OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean now depends on (its new isEnabled filter exists precisely because wrapped models can be disabled) are all skipped, so disabled org-linked IDPs appear on the org login page on warm requests and disappear on cold ones.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows getForLogin() applies createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel() on *delegate* return paths (when cache is invalid or when it has to fall back due to missing IDs), while the cached path resolves each IDP via session.identityProviders().getById(id). This pattern strongly implies getById() already returns the appropriately wrapped/organization-aware model (otherwise getByOrganization(), which also returns models without an explicit wrapping step, would already have been inconsistent). The finding’s claim that getById returns a raw CachedIdentityProvider and therefore warm-cache results skip wrapping is not verifiable from the diff and is contradicted by the added wrapping on only the delegate paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Both cleanup registrations use the literal alias "alias" (testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) instead of the created alias "idp-alias-" + i, so every one of the 21 created IDPs is registered for cleanup under a nonexistent alias. get("alias") returns null and the method reference throws NPE during test cleanup (or silently removes nothing), leaving 21 orphaned IDPs in the shared TEST_REALM_NAME that pollute every subsequent test in the suite; the test itself passes while the realm is left corrupted.

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, after creating each IDP in the loop the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` instead of using the created alias (`"idp-alias-" + i`). The same incorrect literal is used again after creating `idp-alias-20`. This means cleanup will attempt to remove an IDP with alias literally `"alias"` (likely 404/no-op), and the created IDPs won’t be removed, polluting the shared realm for subsequent tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The two cache-population branches use inconsistent revisions for addRevisioned: the first-load branch passes startupRevision while the miss-for-new-searchKey branch passes cache.getCurrentCounter(), so the same key can be written with a stale revision relative to invalidations that already occurred. After an invalidation, a subsequent first-load on a node that started before the invalidation re-adds the query with the old startupRevision, resurrecting the pre-invalidation entry so stale IDP lists (e.g. listing an IDP deleted via remove(), which registerIDPLoginInvalidation already invalidated) are served for login until the next full invalidation — stale login IDPs shown to end users.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show an inconsistency in `getForLogin(...)`: when `query == null` it calls `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, but when the cache entry exists yet `searchKey` is missing it calls `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. That is a concrete, diff-grounded concern for how revisioning/versioning is intended to work for the same `cacheKeyForLogin(...)`. However, the finding’s specific failure mode (“resurrecting pre-invalidation entry”, stale IDPs being served after invalidation) depends on `RealmCacheManager.addRevisioned(...)` / invalidation semantics not shown in the diff, so the described bug impact cannot be strictly verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The caching PR silently changes getLoginPredicate() semantics for every implementation (JPA, LDAP, cache) by excluding org-linked IDPs that lack BROKER_PUBLIC, a behavioral change to the login IDP selection contract, not just to cache behavior. Any existing caller of getLoginPredicate()/getForLogin (login page, backchannel logout, admin console IDP listing, custom storage providers) that previously saw org-linked non-public IDPs no longer does after this diff, with no interface versioning or changelog; deployments relying on org-linked IDPs appearing in FetchMode.ALL results change behavior on upgrade.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`, which will filter out org-linked IDPs unless `BROKER_PUBLIC` is true. Because this predicate is in the shared SPI (`server-spi/.../IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java`), it affects all implementations/callers using `getLoginPredicate()`/`getForLogin`, not just the new Infinispan caching added in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`. Whether this is desired is unclear from the diff, but the finding correctly flags a cross-cutting behavioral/contract change beyond cache mechanics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The per-(realm,mode) login cache entry accumulates one embedded searchKey set per organization ever queried, and every query for an organization not yet in the entry does cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) plus a full delegate reload, so in a realm with N organizations the first login page hit per org invalidates and rebuilds the shared entry N times. Realms with many organizations get repeated full IDP reloads (one per new org) and a single unbounded cache value whose size grows with org count and never shrinks; the invalidateObject is also node-local, so concurrent cluster nodes racing to add different searchKeys with parent-based overwrites lose each other's entries, causing repeated cold reloads.

adjudication.rationale: In `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`, the cache key is only `(realm, mode)` (`cacheKeyForLogin(getRealm(), mode)`), while results are stored per `searchKey` inside a single `IdentityProviderListQuery` (using `organizationId` or `""`). When `query != null` but `query.getIDPs(searchKey) == null`, the code does `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and then fully reloads from `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)` to create a new `IdentityProviderListQuery(..., cached, query)` that appears to embed/retain prior search keys. This means the first query for each previously-unseen organization triggers an invalidate+delegate reload, and the single cached value can grow as more `organizationId` values are queried. The cluster-race/node-local aspect is not provable from this diff alone, but the repeated reload and unbounded per-org accumulation behavior is directly grounded in the shown logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] remove() now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) (an uncached delegate hit) even on the previously cache-served path, adding a storage round-trip to every IDP removal. Every remove() on any node pays an extra delegate lookup; more importantly the fetched storedIdp is passed to registerIDPLoginInvalidation, and if the alias key was cached-and-stale relative to the org link the predicate test runs against the wrong org state, deciding invalidation on outdated data.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make `remove(String alias)` always execute `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)` (new code in `remove()`), whereas previously the delegate lookup only happened on the invalid-cache path. That is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/extra round-trip concern. However, the claim that this causes invalidation decisions to be made on “wrong/outdated org state” is not supported by the diff: the invalidation predicate is run on `storedIdp` fetched from the delegate (not the cached alias entry), so it is not using a stale cached org link here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both cache-miss paths apply it, producing different results for identical queries depending on cache state. On the first (uncached) request the caller receives organization-aware wrapped IDP models (with org-specific config/behavior), and on every subsequent cached request it receives unwrapped delegate models, so login page behavior (e.g. organization-scoped broker config) silently changes between the first and later requests until invalidation — a direct intent drift for a caching layer whose contract is transparency.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `getForLogin(FetchMode mode, String organizationId)` implementation, both cache-miss paths return wrapped models: when `isInvalid(cacheKey)` it does `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, and when populating the cache it also derives IDs from `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)` (which is then used later to resolve models). However, on the cache-hit path it rebuilds results via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns `identityProviders.stream()` without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. This makes the returned model type/behavior depend on cache state, which violates cache transparency and matches the finding’s claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In create(), registerIDPLoginInvalidation evaluates getLoginPredicate() on the incoming model, whose OrganizationId is set only after the organization provider links it via OrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider / the org update path that bypasses this provider's update() (the org link mutates the IDP through the organization API), so no invalidation of the login caches occurs when an existing IDP is linked to or unlinked from an organization. Linking/unlinking an IDP to an organization through the organization management API leaves stale getForLogin caches: FetchMode.ORG_ONLY/ALL queries keep returning (or omitting) the IDP until some unrelated invalidation, so organization login pages show stale broker lists; the test only passes because step 4 mutates BROKER_PUBLIC config (which does invalidate) immediately before addIdentityProvider.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows login-cache invalidation being triggered from this provider’s create/update/remove methods, plus caching in getForLogin. It does not show how OrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider is implemented or whether it calls back into IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update/remove (which would hit registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate and invalidate on organizationId changes). The finding’s claim that the test “only passes because step 4 mutates BROKER_PUBLIC config (which does invalidate)” is also not supported by the diff: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate explicitly avoids invalidation when both original/updated satisfy getLoginPredicate() and organizationId is unchanged, and in step 4 BROKER_PUBLIC changes while organizationId is still null, so this update would not necessarily invalidate. Therefore the asserted stale-cache bug via the org-management API cannot be verified from the provided diff and includes a misread of the invalidation conditions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new predicate conjunct dereferences idp.getConfig().get(...) without a null guard, and the same lambda is also executed in registerIDPLoginInvalidation on the create() path where a caller-supplied model can carry a null config map. An IdentityProviderModel with a null config (constructible via constructor without config) causes NullPointerException inside getLoginPredicate wherever the filter is applied (e.g. getForLogin on any storage provider, or the cache provider's create/update invalidation), breaking IDP creation and login queries with a 500.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new conjunct in `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` that calls `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` without a null-check on `getConfig()` (server-spi `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java`). If `getConfig()` can ever be null for an IDP with a non-null `organizationId`, that would NPE. However, the diff does not show the `IdentityProviderModel` contract/constructors to verify that `getConfig()` may be null in practice, so the finding’s claim that this definitively “breaks IDP creation and login queries with a 500” is not fully verifiable from the diff alone. It is still a concrete robustness issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup registration uses the literal alias "alias" instead of the actual alias "idp-alias-" + i, so the cleanup closure fetches a nonexistent resource for every created IDP. Test teardown calls remove() on an IdentityProviderResource for a nonexistent alias, producing a 404/exception during cleanup and leaking all 20+ created IDPs between tests in the realm, which corrupts subsequent count-based assertions.

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin()`, after creating each IDP with alias `"idp-alias-" + i`, the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (and again after creating `idp-alias-20`). This uses the literal string "alias" instead of the created alias, so the cleanup targets a non-existent IDP resource and will not remove the created IDPs, potentially causing teardown failures and test data leakage across runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new predicate link dereferences idp.getConfig() without a null check, so any IdentityProviderModel with a null config map throws NullPointerException when getForLogin is invoked. The login predicate is applied to every IdentityProviderModel returned from storage on every getForLogin call; an IDP persisted without a config map (or a storage provider returning a model with null config) turns the realm's login page into a 500 error, a denial of the entire login flow for that realm. The legacy filters never dereferenced config unconditionally here, so this is newly introduced on this line.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to add `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`. This unconditionally dereferences `idp.getConfig()` and then calls `.get(...)` on it. If any `IdentityProviderModel` instance has a null config map (e.g., from a custom storage provider or an older persisted record), this predicate will throw `NullPointerException` during `getForLogin(...)` filtering, potentially breaking the login flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getForLogin caches per-(realm, FetchMode) but stores results for an unbounded set of organizationIds in one IdentityProviderListQuery under a key that does not include the organizationId, and on a cache hit the stored set is served without any re-validation that the IDPs are still login-eligible. A realm with many organizations accumulates per-org ID lists in a single shared cache entry; more importantly, if any mutation path updates an IDP through a code path that does not route through InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.update/remove/create (e.g., organization link changes performed directly against the delegate or via bulk import/migration), stale cached lists serve disabled or org-private (BROKER_PUBLIC=false) brokers on the public login page, exposing identity-provider metadata the admin intended to hide and letting users initiate logins with providers that were disabled for the org. The invalidation logic in registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate is only consulted on the update() path of this wrapper, so the cache correctness for login visibility is only as strong as that single choke point.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a per-(realm, FetchMode) cache key for getForLogin via cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode) that does not include organizationId, while IdentityProviderListQuery is populated with a per-searchKey entry where searchKey is derived from organizationId (organizationId != null ? organizationId : ""). When a new organizationId is queried, the code rebuilds the query and chains the previous query (new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query)), implying the single cached object can accumulate results for multiple orgIds over time under one cache key. Also, on cache hits it only checks that each IDP still resolves by id (idp != null) and does not re-apply the login predicate/eligibility filters, so cache correctness relies on invalidations rather than re-validation. However, the finding’s stronger claim about bypassing invalidation via delegate/bulk import paths cannot be verified from this diff alone, so it’s better treated as a scope/architecture concern rather than a proven bug here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup registration looks up IDP alias "alias", which does not exist, instead of "idp-alias-" + i. testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") returns null, so the method reference ::remove throws NullPointerException during test cleanup — and none of the 20 created IDPs are actually removed, polluting the realm for subsequent tests in the class. Same bug repeats at the idp-alias-20 creation site (~line 419).

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, each created IDP has alias `"idp-alias-" + i`, but cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);`, which targets the literal alias `"alias"` instead of the created IDP. The same pattern appears again for `idp-alias-20`. This means the created IDPs are not cleaned up (and the cleanup likely fails/404s), polluting the realm for later tests. The specific claim about `get(...)` returning null and causing an NPE isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the alias mismatch and resulting broken cleanup is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Every getForLogin() call in the test discards its return value; the test asserts only internal cache-query sizes, never the contents of the stream getForLogin returns. If getForLogin returns the wrong providers (e.g., disabled IDPs included because createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel loses the enabled flag, or wrong FetchMode filtering, or wrong org mapping), the test still passes — it verifies the cache machinery, not the cached behavior the PR claims to add. The assertEquals(5/10/11, query.getIDPs(...).size()) assertions are performed on the cache object, a mirror of the implementation's internal representation, not on the API contract.

adjudication.rationale: The new test `testCacheIDPForLogin` invokes `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` several times but never consumes the returned `Stream` (no terminal operation). While `getForLogin` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider` does substantial eager work before returning (e.g., `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(...).collect(Collectors.toSet())`, and it builds `identityProviders` in a loop), the test’s assertions are exclusively against the internal cache artifact `IdentityProviderListQuery` and its stored ID set sizes (e.g., `assertEquals(5, identityProviderListQuery.getIDPs(...).size())`). This validates the cache bookkeeping/representation rather than the API contract/behavior of the returned providers (e.g., enabled/disabled correctness or filtering), so regressions in returned content could slip through even if the internal cache matches expectations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The stale-cache-entry fallback branch in getForLogin (cached id resolves to a null IDP → invalidate cacheKey and re-delegate) has no test triggering it. A regression in this recovery path (e.g., infinite inconsistency or wrong invalidation) would ship unverified; the only test in the diff (OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin) never leaves a dangling internalId in the cache. Checked: testsuite/integration-arquillian/.../cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java is the only test file in the diff and never exercises this branch.

adjudication.rationale: The new `getForLogin` caching logic in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin` has an explicit recovery path when a cached internalId resolves to `null` (`if (idp == null) { realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKey); return idpDelegate.getForLogin(...); }`). The added test `OrganizationCacheTest#testCacheIDPForLogin` verifies cache population and invalidation for create/update/remove scenarios, but it never creates a situation where the cached `Set<String> cached` contains an internalId that no longer exists (a “dangling” ID). E.g., it removes `idp-alias-1` (disabled, thus not part of the cached login sets) and creates/updates `idp-alias-20` while it is `hideOnLogin=true` (also not part of cached login sets), so the `idp == null` fallback branch is not exercised. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test issue for newly added nontrivial recovery logic, not a proven functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The multi-search branch (query exists but query.getIDPs(searchKey) returns null for a new searchKey, triggering invalidateObject + re-load with the old query as parent) is never exercised by the new test. Every test call uses one searchKey per FetchMode ("" for REALM_ONLY, orgaId for ORG_ONLY/ALL), so the branch that merges a second search result into an existing IdentityProviderListQuery is untested; a defect there (e.g., wrong revision counter passed to addRevisioned — note it uses cache.getCurrentCounter() while the first path uses startupRevision) only manifests in production when a realm serves two different organizations, and operators get stale or missing IDP lists on the login page.

adjudication.rationale: The new cache-multi-search path in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin` (when `query != null` but `query.getIDPs(searchKey) == null`, causing `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and rebuilding `IdentityProviderListQuery` with the old query as parent, then `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`) is only exercised if the same `FetchMode` cache key is queried with a *different* `organizationId`/`searchKey` after the first population. In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, each `FetchMode` is only queried with a single `searchKey` ("" for `REALM_ONLY`, and `orgaId` for `ORG_ONLY`/`ALL`), so that branch is never hit. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test coverage issue for newly added nontrivial caching logic; the mention of the counter difference is plausible but not provably a bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new LoginFilter predicate clause excluding org-linked IDPs without BROKER_PUBLIC is verified only for the positive case; the diff's test links only BROKER_PUBLIC=true IDPs to the organization, so no test asserts an org-linked, non-public IDP is (or is not) excluded from any FetchMode. The semantic change that a non-public org broker is now hidden even from FetchMode.REALM_ONLY/ALL listings is untested; if the intended behavior differs per FetchMode (e.g., REALM_ONLY should still surface it for email-domain matching on the realm login page), no test in this diff would catch it. Checked OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin — it creates no org-linked, non-BROKER_PUBLIC IDP.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new clause to `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` requiring `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || BROKER_PUBLIC == true`, which changes which IDPs qualify for `getForLogin(...)` across fetch modes. In `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`, the only IDPs linked to an organization (i=10..19) are all configured with `OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC=true`, so there is no coverage for an org-linked IDP with `BROKER_PUBLIC` missing/false being excluded. This is a specific missing test for newly added nontrivial predicate logic, not a directly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Step 2 (non-availability-changing updates) asserts only that the login cache entries still exist, never that a subsequent getForLogin returns the updated IDP data (e.g., the trustEmail/config change) read through the surviving cache. If the skipped login-cache invalidation combined with per-IDP cache staleness returned outdated IDP models, this test passes because it never re-invokes getForLogin after the update; the caching-correctness guarantee the PR's javadoc for registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate claims ("no need to invalidate" implies data stays correct) is asserted only via cache-object presence, not via behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The new test `testCacheIDPForLogin` Step 2 updates two IDPs (e.g., `setTrustEmail(true)` / config changes) and then only asserts that the `IdentityProviderListQuery` entries for `cacheKeyForLogin(...)` are still present (`assertNotNull`). It does not re-run `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` after those updates to verify that the returned `IdentityProviderModel`s reflect the updated fields while the login-query cache survives. This is a specific gap given the new optimization in `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(...)` that deliberately skips login-cache invalidation in some update scenarios, but the test does not assert behavioral correctness of that choice—only cache-object existence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] On a cache hit, getForLogin returns raw models from session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so cached and uncached code paths return different model types. The two cold paths (isInvalid branch and the idp==null fallback) wrap each model with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, but the cache-hit loop at lines ~246-252 does not; once the login list query is cached, login pages served from cache receive non-organization-aware IdentityProviderModel instances while the first request after invalidation receives wrapped ones — any behavior that depends on the wrapper (org-specific presentation/config) silently differs depending on whether the cache is warm, producing intermittent, unreproducible login-page behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In the new override `getForLogin(FetchMode mode, String organizationId)`, the two delegate (cold) paths explicitly wrap results with `.map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)` (the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch and the `idp == null` fallback). However, on a cache hit it iterates cached internal IDs, loads each model via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)`, adds them to `identityProviders`, and returns `identityProviders.stream()` without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. Nothing in the diff shows `getById` performs that wrapping, so the cached vs uncached paths can return different `IdentityProviderModel` implementations/types and potentially different behavior depending on cache warmth.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new predicate dereferences idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) without a null guard, and the predicate now silently swallows the org-linked check when BROKER_PUBLIC is set to any non-'true' string. For an IDP with organizationId != null and a null config map (IdentityProviderModel.getConfig returns null when unset in some storage/load paths), getLoginPredicate throws NPE inside getForLogin, registerIDPLoginInvalidation, and registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate — breaking IDP create/update/remove operations with a 500. Additionally, Boolean.parseBoolean means config values like "TRUE " or a legacy non-canonical value silently exclude an IDP the admin believes is public, with no log or error; the IDP just disappears from login with no diagnostic.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to call `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` without guarding `getConfig()` against null: `idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(...))`. If any `IdentityProviderModel` has a null config map, this predicate will throw an NPE anywhere it’s used (notably in the newly added `registerIDPLoginInvalidation*` methods that call `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)`, and in `getForLogin`). The `Boolean.parseBoolean` behavior about non-canonical strings is true but more of an ergonomics concern than a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In remove(), the stored IDP is fetched via idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) before checking isInvalid(cacheKey), but the registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) on line ~112 only fires when the currently-stored model still satisfies getLoginPredicate, which reads through the delegate — and the predicate's new BROKER_PUBLIC clause means an org-linked IDP whose BROKER_PUBLIC config is absent is treated as not-a-login-IDP and its removal skips login-cache invalidation. Removing an org-linked IDP that was previously returned by getForLogin(FetchMode.ALL/ORG_ONLY) via a path where BROKER_PUBLIC was true at cache-population time but the predicate now evaluates it as ineligible leaves stale internal IDs in the login list query; the cached path's getById==null fallback mitigates it, but only after the cache is read and the fallback triggers a delegate reload — meanwhile getIDPs() consumers of the cached query (and any cross-node replica where the invalidation hasn't propagated) observe the removed IDP as present until then.

adjudication.rationale: The claim hinges on an IDP being present in the new getForLogin() caches while simultaneously failing the new getLoginPredicate() (due to missing BROKER_PUBLIC) so that remove() would skip invalidation and leave stale IDs. But in this diff, the same updated predicate (with the BROKER_PUBLIC/org-link clause) is what determines “login IDP” eligibility, and getForLogin() caches are populated from idpDelegate.getForLogin(...), so an org-linked IDP with BROKER_PUBLIC absent would not be fetched/cached in the first place. Additionally, updates that change eligibility (e.g., toggling/removing BROKER_PUBLIC or org link) are handled by registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(), which invalidates in the non-preserving cases. The finding also incorrectly states the predicate “reads through the delegate”; it just tests the provided model. The described stale-cache scenario is not verifiable from the diff alone.
